title: An NCG mouse model of Hantaan virus reveals systemic infection and organ-specific cellular tropism.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Following viral inoculation, we assessed viral loads via quantitative RT-PCR and mapped cellular tropism and co-localization of HTNV with potential receptors using immunofluorescence staining.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The mechanisms of HTNV infection remain poorly understood, largely due to the lack of susceptible animal models.
analysis.methods: In this study, we established a systemic HTNV infection mouse model using highly immunodeficient NCG mice.
analysis.main_results: Co-localization analyses indicated HTNV infection might be associated with distinct entry receptors across target organs: potentially ITGB1 and gC1qR in specific renal cells, and ITGB1 and ITGB2 in pulmonary AT1 cells and macrophages, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: HTNV exhibited distinct organ-specific cellular tropism in vivo, predominantly targeting fibroblasts and interstitial cells of the renal collecting duct in the kidney, alveolar epithelial cells and macrophages in the lung, and broadly infecting multiple cell populations in the brain and ovary.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings demonstrate that NCG mouse is a valuable in vivo model for studying HTNV replication and systemic dissemination.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: While histopathological lesions were subclinical, HTNV-infected NCG mice exhibited robust viremia and sustained viral replication across multiple organs, including the kidney, lung, spleen, reproductive organs, and liver.

analysis.summary_en: Following viral inoculation, we assessed viral loads via quantitative RT-PCR and mapped cellular tropism and co-localization of HTNV with potential receptors using immunofluorescence staining. The mechanisms of HTNV infection remain poorly understood, largely due to the lack of susceptible animal models. In this study, we established a systemic HTNV infection mouse model using highly immunodeficient NCG mice. Co-localization analyses indicated HTNV infection might be associated with distinct entry receptors across target organs: potentially ITGB1 and gC1qR in specific renal cells, and ITGB1 and ITGB2 in pulmonary AT1 cells and macrophages, respectively. HTNV exhibited distinct organ-specific cellular tropism in vivo, predominantly targeting fibroblasts and interstitial cells of the renal collecting duct in the kidney, alveolar epithelial cells and macrophages in the lung, and broadly infecting multiple cell populations in the brain and ovary. These findings demonstrate that NCG mouse is a valuable in vivo model for studying HTNV replication and systemic dissemination. While histopathological lesions were subclinical, HTNV-infected NCG mice exhibited robust viremia and sustained viral replication across multiple organs, including the kidney, lung, spleen, reproductive organs, and liver.

title: Assessing the performance of time series prediction models for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome across different high-risk areas in Shaanxi Province, China

analysis.research_question_and_background: Background Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a climate-sensitive disease.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study compares time series models incorporating environmental factors for prefecture-level HFRS prediction.
analysis.methods: Methods Monthly HFRS case counts and 14 environmental factors were collected from 2005 to 2023 in four typical prefecture-level cities, including Xi'an, Baoji, Xianyang, and Weinan.
analysis.main_results: In Xi'an and Baoji, the multivariate LSTMX model showed lower forecasting errors (Xi'an: R 2 = 0.976, RMSE decreased from 69.246 to 17.782; Baoji: R 2 = 0.950, RMSE decreased from 6.694 to 2.805).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Pairwise model differences were not statistically significant after Holm correction, and the city ranking changed when the models were refitted on the monthly crude incidence-rate scale; the rankings are therefore reported descriptively and are not interpreted as evidence of regional differences in environmental effects.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Conclusions No single forecasting configuration was uniformly optimal across cities: LSTMX with lagged environmental factors yielded the lowest errors in Xi'an and Baoji, whereas univariate models yielded lower errors in Xianyang and Weinan; however, these pairwise differences did not reach statistical significance after Holm correction and changed under the incidence-rate scale.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: When extending these models to new settings, both univariate and covariate-enhanced configurations should be compared.

analysis.summary_en: Background Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a climate-sensitive disease. This study compares time series models incorporating environmental factors for prefecture-level HFRS prediction. Methods Monthly HFRS case counts and 14 environmental factors were collected from 2005 to 2023 in four typical prefecture-level cities, including Xi'an, Baoji, Xianyang, and Weinan. In Xi'an and Baoji, the multivariate LSTMX model showed lower forecasting errors (Xi'an: R 2 = 0.976, RMSE decreased from 69.246 to 17.782; Baoji: R 2 = 0.950, RMSE decreased from 6.694 to 2.805). Pairwise model differences were not statistically significant after Holm correction, and the city ranking changed when the models were refitted on the monthly crude incidence-rate scale; the rankings are therefore reported descriptively and are not interpreted as evidence of regional differences in environmental effects. Conclusions No single forecasting configuration was uniformly optimal across cities: LSTMX with lagged environmental factors yielded the lowest errors in Xi'an and Baoji, whereas univariate models yielded lower errors in Xianyang and Weinan; however, these pairwise differences did not reach statistical significance after Holm correction and changed under the incidence-rate scale. When extending these models to new settings, both univariate and covariate-enhanced configurations should be compared.

title: Case Report: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome caused by Seoul orthohantavirus mimicking severe acute pancreatitis: dynamic imaging evolution and pathogen confirmation by mNGS

analysis.research_question_and_background: He already had profound thrombocytopenia on admission (nadir 29 × 109/L), progressive renal impairment, hematuria, and proteinuria, without typical pancreatitis risk factors or elevated pancreatic enzymes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: DiscussionThis case highlights a diagnostically challenging presentation in which Seoul orthohantavirus infection clinically and radiologically mimicked severe acute pancreatitis, underscoring the need to consider HFRS in the differential diagnosis of unexplained pancreatitis-like presentations (1).
analysis.methods: Whole-blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected high-copy Seoul orthohantavirus, with concurrent hepatitis B virus.
analysis.main_results: Initial non-contrast abdominal CT showed peripancreatic and perirenal haziness, renal fascial thickening, and small-volume abdominopelvic effusion with mild pancreatic swelling, findings highly suggestive of severe acute pancreatitis (Figure 1).Figure 1Serial axial abdominal computed tomography (CT) images of Seoul orthohantavirus-associated capillary-leak syndrome mimicking severe acute pancreatitis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The patient recovered fully with supportive care, intravenous immunoglobulin, and symptomatic treatment; pre-discharge ultrasound showed normal pancreatic morphology.ConclusionSeoul orthohantavirus infection can closely mimic severe acute pancreatitis clinically and radiologically.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Reticulocyte count was not tested in clinical practice; hemoglobin levels over serial time-points are presented to evaluate for bone-marrow suppression.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Although viral gastroenteritis could explain fever, vomiting and watery diarrhea, the presence of epigastric tenderness on physical examination together with marked peripancreatic-perirenal exudates identified on initial abdominal CT raised strong clinical suspicion for severe acute pancreatitis.

analysis.summary_en: He already had profound thrombocytopenia on admission (nadir 29 × 109/L), progressive renal impairment, hematuria, and proteinuria, without typical pancreatitis risk factors or elevated pancreatic enzymes. DiscussionThis case highlights a diagnostically challenging presentation in which Seoul orthohantavirus infection clinically and radiologically mimicked severe acute pancreatitis, underscoring the need to consider HFRS in the differential diagnosis of unexplained pancreatitis-like presentations (1). Whole-blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected high-copy Seoul orthohantavirus, with concurrent hepatitis B virus. Initial non-contrast abdominal CT showed peripancreatic and perirenal haziness, renal fascial thickening, and small-volume abdominopelvic effusion with mild pancreatic swelling, findings highly suggestive of severe acute pancreatitis (Figure 1).Figure 1Serial axial abdominal computed tomography (CT) images of Seoul orthohantavirus-associated capillary-leak syndrome mimicking severe acute pancreatitis. The patient recovered fully with supportive care, intravenous immunoglobulin, and symptomatic treatment; pre-discharge ultrasound showed normal pancreatic morphology.ConclusionSeoul orthohantavirus infection can closely mimic severe acute pancreatitis clinically and radiologically. Reticulocyte count was not tested in clinical practice; hemoglobin levels over serial time-points are presented to evaluate for bone-marrow suppression. Although viral gastroenteritis could explain fever, vomiting and watery diarrhea, the presence of epigastric tenderness on physical examination together with marked peripancreatic-perirenal exudates identified on initial abdominal CT raised strong clinical suspicion for severe acute pancreatitis.

title: Immature Platelet Fraction in Viral Infections: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives

analysis.scope_and_question: Reticulated platelets, reported by modern hematology analyzers as the immature platelet fraction (IPF%) or the absolute immature platelet count (IPC), index thrombopoiesis and have been proposed as biomarkers in the thrombocytopenia of viral infection.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2000 to May 2025 for observational studies of adults with viral infection reporting IPF, IPC, or reticulated platelets, and methodological robustness was appraised with the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Applications differed by pathogen: in dengue, serial IPF increases consistently preceded platelet recovery, although proposed thresholds varied; in COVID-19, higher immature platelet parameters were associated with severity and mortality but were inconsistent after adjustment.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Analytical heterogeneity and the absence of transferable thresholds currently limit clinical implementation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Clinical value appears disease- and outcome-specific: serial IPF best predicts platelet recovery in dengue, whereas prognostic use in COVID-19 remains insufficiently validated.

analysis.summary_en: Reticulated platelets, reported by modern hematology analyzers as the immature platelet fraction (IPF%) or the absolute immature platelet count (IPC), index thrombopoiesis and have been proposed as biomarkers in the thrombocytopenia of viral infection. PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2000 to May 2025 for observational studies of adults with viral infection reporting IPF, IPC, or reticulated platelets, and methodological robustness was appraised with the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale. Applications differed by pathogen: in dengue, serial IPF increases consistently preceded platelet recovery, although proposed thresholds varied; in COVID-19, higher immature platelet parameters were associated with severity and mortality but were inconsistent after adjustment. Analytical heterogeneity and the absence of transferable thresholds currently limit clinical implementation. Clinical value appears disease- and outcome-specific: serial IPF best predicts platelet recovery in dengue, whereas prognostic use in COVID-19 remains insufficiently validated.

title: Reverse Vaccinology Design of an Asian HLA-Targeted Multi-Epitope Vaccine Candidate Against HTNV Strain 76-118

analysis.research_question_and_background: HTNV remains a cause of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, particularly in Asia, while broadly available vaccines remain limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study developed an Asian HLA-targeted multi-epitope vaccine candidate against HTNV strain 76-118 using reverse vaccinology and immunoinformatics.
analysis.methods: RdRp, GPC, and N proteins were screened for cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL), helper T-lymphocyte (HTL), and linear B-cell epitopes using 42 representative Asian HLA alleles.
analysis.main_results: Combined MHC class I and II predicted coverage averaged 95.15% across five regions and reached 99.29% in East Asia.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Docking with TLR4 yielded a predicted ΔG of −27.6 kcal mol−1, while trajectory-based MM-GBSA analysis produced a ΔGbind of −136.17 ± 3.14 kcal mol−1.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Codon optimization achieved a CAI of 0.9640 and GC content of 52.27%.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Collectively, these computational analyses identify the HBHA-based construct as a population-oriented HTNV vaccine candidate prioritized for subsequent experimental evaluation.

analysis.summary_en: HTNV remains a cause of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, particularly in Asia, while broadly available vaccines remain limited. This study developed an Asian HLA-targeted multi-epitope vaccine candidate against HTNV strain 76-118 using reverse vaccinology and immunoinformatics. RdRp, GPC, and N proteins were screened for cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL), helper T-lymphocyte (HTL), and linear B-cell epitopes using 42 representative Asian HLA alleles. Combined MHC class I and II predicted coverage averaged 95.15% across five regions and reached 99.29% in East Asia. Docking with TLR4 yielded a predicted ΔG of −27.6 kcal mol−1, while trajectory-based MM-GBSA analysis produced a ΔGbind of −136.17 ± 3.14 kcal mol−1. Codon optimization achieved a CAI of 0.9640 and GC content of 52.27%. Collectively, these computational analyses identify the HBHA-based construct as a population-oriented HTNV vaccine candidate prioritized for subsequent experimental evaluation.
